cells.tense: Right now something concrete sits in your hands and it hasn't been handed on or handed over.
cells.act: give a concrete piece of help and finish it
cells.ask: Someone near you is stuck on a task you can do. Do the actual work for them this week — beginning to end — and when it's finished, stop. No reasons offered, no explanation of why you bothered.
cells.core:
You can pick a direction and mean it. When you choose this and not that, the choice keeps its shape, and whoever stands nearby feels the floor under them. That isn't force; it's intention that stopped wobbling. There is something you've kept at the starting line — a commitment, a resource, a yes you've half-given — and keeping it there is no longer doubt. It's readiness nobody has spent yet.

What this balance is free to feed next is somebody else's start. Give one person real help on something they're genuinely stuck on, something within your reach — not advice, not a name to call, the work itself, with a beginning and an end. Finish it, then leave it. Help lands hardest when it doesn't arrive with a bill of reasons attached.

cells.verb: starting a thing that is now yours to actually begin

cells.tense: Tomorrow is getting sketched out while this afternoon still hasn't been finished.
cells.act: know the feeling fully before you move on
cells.ask: Before you take one more next step today, put the whole of it on paper — every feeling in it, nothing crossed out, nothing edited — and only then move on.
cells.core:
You direct things, and lately the direction arrives faster than the ground it stands on. Something is barely begun and you've already mapped the version after it — the next commitment, the next use for it — and the mapping feels like momentum. Some of it is. Some of it is bracing: writing the future because the present hasn't been finished off, and finishing it would mean feeling all of what's here. The push gets faster the less you let yourself know.

There's another way to do this without slowing the direction down. Let the feeling be complete before you act on the next step. Whatever the thing you're holding actually feels like, let it finish feeling like that — the whole of it, all at once — and then choose. Direction chosen after that lands in real ground.

cells.tense: There was a direction you picked once, and picking it stopped at the door.
cells.act: lay every piece of it out where you can see all of it at once
cells.ask: Take the thing you keep circling and spread its parts out somewhere you can see them together — on paper, a table, the floor. Stay there a while.
cells.core:
The ability to choose is here, but it isn't arriving. Something concrete is ready to begin and the yes hasn't been said — not refused, just not yet — and standing still has a shape to it, like waiting in a doorway you're already through. Nobody watching would call it stuck. They'd call it thinking. It's the thinking standing in for the move.

Refilling this doesn't take more effort. It takes seeing a whole situation at once — every part of it, spread out where nothing hides — until the last of the fog is gone. Once you can see the full picture, choosing stops being a cliff and becomes a step. Look at the thing you keep circling until the fog has cleared. The yes gets easy after that, not before.

cells.tense: Direction is getting chosen in this room and the chooser keeps saying it just happened.
cells.act: see it whole, with nothing hidden
cells.ask: Next time something shifts because of you, don't hand it to luck. Look at the actual thing you did, in order, whole and unhidden — just to yourself, just once.
cells.core:
You steer, and the account you give is circumstance. A thing got built, a thing got started, a thing got turned around — and the story is that it went that way by itself, or someone else did it, or the timing was kind. The steering is happening. The credit for it gets filed as luck. The people nearest you have watched it happen and stopped being surprised.

Seeing your own hand is the simplest form of the same clarity: look at the whole thing, nothing hidden, as your own doing. Take the next shift that happens because of you and look at what you actually did, step by step, without reaching for the humbler story. Not a boast. Just the honest record. That is how the next choice becomes a choice, instead of something that happened to you.

attempts.check: The record has no fact about what this person has actually built or why nothing is finished, so any claim about their history (a past launch, a disappointment) would be invented. The reader could reasonably say 'I direct things just fine' — so every cell must pass the say-no test: it describes a moment, not their character.
